def CRel (k : K) (C : CState) : COp → Outcome3 CState → Prop
  | .derive a r m => LiftR (OpRel k C.toL (.derive a r m)) C.setL
  | .split a rs => LiftR (OpRel k C.toL (.split a rs)) C.setL
  | .release a => LiftR (OpRel k C.toL (.release a)) C.setL
  | .transfer a b => LiftR (OpRel k C.toL (.transfer a b)) C.setL
  | .depend q x => LiftR (OpRel k C.toL (.depend q x)) C.setL
  | .enter ps ls => LiftR (OpRel k C.toL (.enter ps ls)) C.setL
  | .exit => LiftR (OpRel k C.toL .exit) C.setL
  | .read a ls => LiftR (OpRel k C.toL (.read a ls)) C.setL
  | .write a ls => LiftR (OpRel k C.toL (.write a ls)) C.setL
  | .writeShared a ls => LiftR (OpRel k C.toL (.writeShared a ls)) C.setL
  | .pin p => LiftR (OpRel k C.toL (.pin p)) C.setL
  | .unpin o => LiftR (OpRel k C.toL (.unpin o)) C.setL
  | .endUse p => LiftR (OpRel k C.toL (.endUse p)) C.setL
  | .free p a => LiftR (OpRel k C.toL (.free p a)) C.setL
  | .alloc pr ow ls => LiftR (OpRel k C.toL (.alloc pr ow ls)) C.setL
  | .store a p => LiftR (OpRel k C.toL (.store a p)) C.setL
  | .newArena st i => LiftR (NewArenaStep C.othersA st i C.toL) C.setL
  | .issue i r d => LiftR (OpRel k C.toL (.issue i r d)) C.setL
  | .reset i => LiftR (OpRel k C.toL (.reset i)) C.setL
  | .newPool st i => LiftR (HandlePool.NewPoolStep C.othersP st i C.toP) C.setP
  | .allocSlot j d => LiftR (HandlePool.AllocSlotStep j d C.toP) C.setP
  | .resolve j h m => LiftR (HandlePool.ResolveStep j h m C.toP) C.setP
  | .resolveMany j hs m => LiftR (HandlePool.ResolveManyStep k j hs m C.toP) C.setP
  | .unresolve c => LiftR (HandlePool.UnresolveStep c C.toP) C.setP
  | .freeSlot j h => LiftR (HandlePool.FreeSlotStep j h C.toP) C.setP
  | .newStack st i => LiftR (DataStack.NewStackStep C.othersD st i C.toD) C.setD
  | .push j n d => LiftR (DataStack.PushStep k j n d C.toD) C.setD
  | .mark j => LiftR (DataStack.MarkStep j C.toD) C.setD
  | .rewind j m => LiftR (DataStack.RewindStep k j m C.toD) C.setD
  | .grow j b e => LiftR (DataStack.GrowStep k j b e C.toD) C.setD

/-! ## Executor -/

/-- The first free slot of a slot list and its index (HandlePool v0.5, D.3: "`ok` choisit un
slot libre"; the lowest index is chosen, one of the outcomes the relation allows). -/
def firstFree : List HandlePool.Slot → Option (Nat × HandlePool.Slot)
  | [] => none
  | sl :: l => if sl.live then (firstFree l).map fun p => (p.1 + 1, p.2) else some (0, sl)

/-- An authority that can write the leaf `dst` (§67), searched among the authorities of `s`. -/
def writer (s : S3) (dst : Nat) : Option Nat :=
  (List.range s.A.length).find? fun a => decide (Write3Pre s a [dst])

/-- The kernel-side check of a step of `crun` (§67; HandlePool v0.5, D.3): the handle write
of `allocSlot` is a kernel `write` by some authority. -/
def COp.kok (C : CState) : COp → Bool
  | .allocSlot _ dst => (writer C.kern dst).isSome
  | _ => true

section Exec
variable (k : K) [∀ r r', Decidable (k.DeclaredDisjoint r r')] [DecidablePred k.SharedMutable]
  [DecidablePred k.Pinned] [DecidablePred k.ExternalDone] [DecidablePred k.Deallocable]
  [∀ p a, Decidable (k.FreeCompat p a)] [∀ p ls s, Decidable (k.Satisfiable p ls s)]

/-- Computed outcome of `allocSlot(pool j, dst)` (HandlePool v0.5, D.3; §58). -/
def allocSlotOut (P : HandlePool.PState) (j dst : Nat) : Outcome3 HandlePool.PState :=
  match P.pools[j]? with
  | none => .reject
  | some pl =>
    if HandlePool.AllocSlotStatic P.kern pl dst then
      match firstFree pl.slots with
      | some (i, sl) => .ok (HandlePool.allocSlotEff P j pl i sl dst)
      | none => .fail
    else .reject

/-- Computed outcome of `resolve(h, m)` on pool `j` (HandlePool v0.5, D.2, HP5-5: the handle is
checked before the right; §58). -/
def resolveOut (P : HandlePool.PState) (j : Nat) (h : HandlePool.Handle) (m : Mode) :
    Outcome3 HandlePool.PState :=
  match P.pools[j]? with
  | none => .reject
  | some pl =>
    if HandlePool.HandleOK P.kern pl h then
      if HandlePool.ResolveRight P.kern pl m then
        match pl.slots[h.slot]? with
        | some sl =>
          if DerivePre (HandlePool.compS P.kern pl m) P.kern.A.length
              (footprint P.kern.P sl.place) m then
            .ok { P with
              kern := deriveEff (HandlePool.compS P.kern pl m) P.kern.A.length
                (footprint P.kern.P sl.place) m
              res := P.res ++ [⟨pl.id, pl.internal, P.kern.A.length, m,
                [(P.kern.A.length + 1, h.slot, h.gen)]⟩] }
          else .reject
        | none => .reject
      else .reject
    else .fail

/-- Computed outcome of `resolveMany(hs, m)` on pool `j` (HandlePool v0.5, D.2, HP5-5: the batch
is checked before the right; §58). -/
def resolveManyOut (P : HandlePool.PState) (j : Nat) (hs : List HandlePool.Handle) (m : Mode) :
    Outcome3 HandlePool.PState :=
  match P.pools[j]? with
  | none => .reject
  | some pl =>
    if HandlePool.BatchOK P.kern pl hs m then
      if HandlePool.ResolveRight P.kern pl m then
        if HandlePool.EntriesPre k m (HandlePool.compS P.kern pl m) P.kern.A.length
            (HandlePool.entryRegions P.kern pl hs) then
          .ok { P with
            kern := HandlePool.entriesEff m (HandlePool.compS P.kern pl m) P.kern.A.length
              (HandlePool.entryRegions P.kern pl hs)
            res := P.res ++ [⟨pl.id, pl.internal, P.kern.A.length, m,
              HandlePool.batchEntries P.kern.A.length hs⟩] }
        else .reject
      else .reject
    else .fail

/-- Computed outcome of `unresolve(c)` (HandlePool v0.5, D.2; §58). -/
def unresolveOut (P : HandlePool.PState) (c : Nat) : Outcome3 HandlePool.PState :=
  match HandlePool.findRes P c with
  | none => .reject
  | some r =>
    match HandlePool.releaseAll P.kern (HandlePool.unresolveList P.kern r) with
    | none => .reject
    | some s' => .ok { P with kern := s' }

/-- Computed outcome of `freeSlot(h)` on pool `j` (HandlePool v0.5, D.3, HP5-1, HP5-1': the
content conditions; outcome order of HP5-1'': the handle, pool liveness included, before the
administration right; §58). -/
def freeSlotOut (P : HandlePool.PState) (j : Nat) (h : HandlePool.Handle) :
    Outcome3 HandlePool.PState :=
  match P.pools[j]? with
  | none => .reject
  | some pl =>
    if HandlePool.HandleOK P.kern pl h then
      if HandlePool.AdminRight P.kern pl then
        match pl.slots[h.slot]? with
        | some sl =>
          if HandlePool.FreeContentOK P pl sl.place then
            .ok (HandlePool.freeSlotEff P j pl h.slot sl)
          else .reject
        | none => .reject
      else .reject
    else .fail

/-- Computed outcome of `push(j, size, dst)` (DS-v2; Part XIV, §77; §58). -/
def pushOut (D : DataStack.DState) (j size dst : Nat) : Outcome3 DataStack.DState :=
  match D.stacks[j]? with
  | none => .reject
  | some st =>
    if IssueStatic D.kern st.entry (DataStack.cellsOf st st.top size) dst then
      if st.top + size ≤ st.cells.length then
        if SplitPre k D.kern st.internal [DataStack.cellsOf st st.top size] then
          if StorePre (splitEff D.kern st.internal [DataStack.cellsOf st st.top size])
              D.kern.A.length dst then
            .ok ⟨storeEff (splitEff D.kern st.internal [DataStack.cellsOf st st.top size])
              D.kern.A.length dst,
              D.stacks.set j (DataStack.pushMeta st size D.kern.A.length dst), D.fresh⟩
          else .reject
        else .reject
      else .fail
    else .reject

/-- Computed outcome of `mark(j)` (DS-v2, DS2-1: `AdminRight` required, §36; §58). -/
def markOut (D : DataStack.DState) (j : Nat) : Outcome3 DataStack.DState :=
  match D.stacks[j]? with
  | none => .reject
  | some st =>
    if DataStack.AdminRight D.kern st then
      .ok ⟨D.kern, D.stacks.set j (DataStack.markMeta j st D.fresh), D.fresh + 1⟩
    else .reject

/-- Computed outcome of `rewind(j, m)` (DS-v2, DS2-3, DS2-4, DS2-6: a missing stack and a dead or
foreign mark `fail` before the right; Part XIV, §78; §58). -/
def rewindOut (D : DataStack.DState) (j : Nat) (m : DataStack.Mark) :
    Outcome3 DataStack.DState :=
  match D.stacks[j]? with
  | none => .fail
  | some st =>
    if DataStack.LiveMark D.kern j st m then
      if DataStack.AdminRight D.kern st then
        if SplitPre k D.kern st.internal [DataStack.above st m] then
          if ReleasePre (splitEff D.kern st.internal [DataStack.above st m])
              D.kern.A.length then
            .ok ⟨releaseEff (splitEff D.kern st.internal [DataStack.above st m])
              D.kern.A.length, D.stacks.set j (DataStack.rewindMeta st m), D.fresh⟩
          else .reject
        else .reject
      else .reject
    else .fail

/-- Computed outcome of `grow(j, b, extra)` (DS-v2, DS2-2: into the place that holds `b`; DS2-5:
`extra` may be zero; Part XIV, §77; §58). -/
def growOut (D : DataStack.DState) (j b extra : Nat) : Outcome3 DataStack.DState :=
  match D.stacks[j]? with
  | none => .reject
  | some st =>
    match st.block b with
    | none => .reject
    | some x =>
      if ReleasePre D.kern b then
        match DataStack.holderPlace D.kern b with
        | none => .reject
        | some d =>
          if IssueStatic (releaseEff D.kern b) st.entry
              (DataStack.cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)) d then
            if DataStack.InPlace st x extra then
              if SplitPre k (releaseEff D.kern b) st.internal
                  [DataStack.cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)] then
                if StorePre (splitEff (releaseEff D.kern b) st.internal
                    [DataStack.cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)])
                    (releaseEff D.kern b).A.length d then
                  .ok ⟨storeEff (splitEff (releaseEff D.kern b) st.internal
                      [DataStack.cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)])
                      (releaseEff D.kern b).A.length d,
                    D.stacks.set j (DataStack.growMeta st x extra (releaseEff D.kern b).A.length d),
                    D.fresh⟩
                else .reject
              else .reject
            else .fail
          else .reject
      else .reject

/-- The computed outcome of `o` from `C` (§58, §60–§78; HandlePool v0.5; DS-v2): the
executor of `Ern.Corpus` on the arena projection for O1–O16, `issue` and `reset`; the guard of §56
over all registries for the creation operations; the pool and stack executors above. -/
def cstep (C : CState) : COp → Outcome3 CState
  | .derive a r m => liftO C.setL (lstep k C.toL (.derive a r m))
  | .split a rs => liftO C.setL (lstep k C.toL (.split a rs))
  | .release a => liftO C.setL (lstep k C.toL (.release a))
  | .transfer a b => liftO C.setL (lstep k C.toL (.transfer a b))
  | .depend q x => liftO C.setL (lstep k C.toL (.depend q x))
  | .enter ps ls => liftO C.setL (lstep k C.toL (.enter ps ls))
  | .exit => liftO C.setL (lstep k C.toL .exit)
  | .read a ls => liftO C.setL (lstep k C.toL (.read a ls))
  | .write a ls => liftO C.setL (lstep k C.toL (.write a ls))
  | .writeShared a ls => liftO C.setL (lstep k C.toL (.writeShared a ls))
  | .pin p => liftO C.setL (lstep k C.toL (.pin p))
  | .unpin o => liftO C.setL (lstep k C.toL (.unpin o))
  | .endUse p => liftO C.setL (lstep k C.toL (.endUse p))
  | .free p a => liftO C.setL (lstep k C.toL (.free p a))
  | .alloc pr ow ls => liftO C.setL (lstep k C.toL (.alloc pr ow ls))
  | .store a p => liftO C.setL (lstep k C.toL (.store a p))
  | .newArena st i =>
    if NewArenaPre C.kern C.arenas C.othersA st i then .ok (C.setL (newArenaEff C.toL st i))
    else .reject
  | .issue i r d => liftO C.setL (lstep k C.toL (.issue i r d))
  | .reset i => liftO C.setL (lstep k C.toL (.reset i))
  | .newPool st i =>
    if HandlePool.NewPoolPre C.kern C.pools C.othersP st i then
      .ok (C.setP (HandlePool.newPoolEff C.toP st i))
    else .reject
  | .allocSlot j d => liftO C.setP (allocSlotOut C.toP j d)
  | .resolve j h m => liftO C.setP (resolveOut C.toP j h m)
  | .resolveMany j hs m => liftO C.setP (resolveManyOut k C.toP j hs m)
  | .unresolve c => liftO C.setP (unresolveOut C.toP c)
  | .freeSlot j h => liftO C.setP (freeSlotOut C.toP j h)
  | .newStack st i =>
    if DataStack.NewStackPre C.kern C.stacks C.othersD st i then
      .ok (C.setD (DataStack.newStackEff C.toD st i))
    else .reject
  | .push j n d => liftO C.setD (pushOut k C.toD j n d)
  | .mark j => liftO C.setD (markOut C.toD j)
  | .rewind j m => liftO C.setD (rewindOut k C.toD j m)
  | .grow j b e => liftO C.setD (growOut k C.toD j b e)

/-- The state after `o` from `C` when it is `ok`; `C` otherwise (§58). -/
def cnext (C : CState) (o : COp) : CState :=
  match cstep k C o with
  | .ok C' => C'
  | _ => C

/-- The state reached by `os` from `C` when every step is `ok` and every `allocSlot` handle write
is a kernel write (§58, §67); `none` otherwise. -/
def crun (C : CState) : List COp → Option CState
  | [] => some C
  | o :: os =>
    match cstep k C o with
    | .ok C' => if o.kok C then crun C' os else none
    | _ => none

/-- The state reached by `os` from `CState.init statics` (§47); `CState.init statics` when the run
does not complete (used only under `(crun …).isSome = true`, see `crunsTo`). -/
def cfinal (statics : Statics) (os : List COp) : CState :=
  (crun k (CState.init statics) os).getD (CState.init statics)

end Exec

/-- Combined library states reachable from `CState.init statics` (§47) by `ok` steps of the kernel
and of the three libraries (Part XIV; HandlePool v0.5; DS-v2). -/
inductive CReach (k : K) (statics : Statics) : CState → Prop where
  | init : CReach k statics (CState.init statics)
  | step {C C' : CState} {o : COp} : CReach k statics C → CRel k C o (.ok C') →
      CReach k statics C'

section Runs
variable (k : K) [∀ r r', Decidable (k.DeclaredDisjoint r r')] [DecidablePred k.SharedMutable]
  [DecidablePred k.Pinned] [DecidablePred k.ExternalDone] [DecidablePred k.Deallocable]
  [∀ p a, Decidable (k.FreeCompat p a)] [∀ p ls s, Decidable (k.Satisfiable p ls s)]

/-- A run of `os` from `CState.init statics` (§47) has only `ok` steps and reaches `C`; `C` is
library-reachable, and its kernel state is reachable by O1–O16 (§57; HandlePool v0.5, HP5-7). -/
structure CRunsTo (statics : Statics) (os : List COp) (C : CState) : Prop where
  /-- Every step is `ok` and the run ends in `C`. -/
  run : crun k (CState.init statics) os = some C
  /-- `C` is library-reachable. -/
  creach : CReach k statics C
  /-- The kernel state of `C` is reachable from `S3.init statics` by O1–O16 (§57). -/
  reach : Reachable k statics C.kern

/-- The run of `os` from `CState.init statics` has only `ok` steps (§47, §57). -/
abbrev CRuns (statics : Statics) (os : List COp) : Prop :=
  CRunsTo k statics os (cfinal k statics os)

end Runs

/-! ## Step soundness (§58) -/

/-- A computed outcome of a projected relation is an outcome of its lift (§58). -/
theorem liftR_liftO {σ : Type} {R : Outcome3 σ → Prop} {emb : σ → CState} {o : Outcome3 σ}
    (h : R o) : LiftR R emb (liftO emb o) := by
  cases o with
  | ok x => exact ⟨x, h, rfl⟩
  | reject => exact h

# ERN — Memory Model Specification v0.1

**Edition v0.1 — corrective candidate, not yet validated**

Modified clauses, relative to v0 (each change is justified by a defect found while formalizing v0):

- §36: `MetaRight` governs authorities over existing storage, not the fresh allocation of `alloc`; §36 and §71.2 contradicted each other.
- §40: `RootHeld` restricted to usable root places, as in §49.7; the two clauses differed on unusable root places.
- §47: the ownership graph of statics is acyclic; a static ownership cycle made §57 false in the initial state.
- §51: a valid origin is an active origin; "valid" was undefined there.
- §57: definition of I5, which v0 named without defining.
- §59: "access operations" are O9–O11; read as all operations, §59 contradicted §69.
- §60.1: a valid origin chain is an active one, read through §44.
- §63.4: the active derived authorities covering the source from outside are named, and the authorities through which the step exercises its `Modify` right are exempt; without this exemption no value could be moved through a derived authority.
- §63.9 (new): the destination is usable in the resulting state; without it an accepted transfer could create an ownership cycle and break §49.8 and §57.
- §69.2 and §70.3: the same exemption as §63.4, and rejection when an authority made inactive by the step keeps an active descendant; without it an accepted step left an active authority with an inactive origin.
- §71.2: the provider is a usable place; v0 did not require it to exist.
- §74 and §75: each `pin` installs an obligation of fresh identity and `unpin` ends one designated obligation; per-leaf pin flags let an `unpin` lift a pin installed by another `pin`.
- §76.6: the reading of the precondition (whole kernel state, `ArenaInv` of the new entry, resulting state); v0 admitted several readings with different verdicts.
- §78.3: restricted to anchors covering a leaf of the administered storage; as written, its second sentence was false.
- §82.2: address and provenance of a pointer to a region whose leaves all have zero physical size; v0 decided no address for that region.
- §86: the last sentence is rewritten; as written, it was false, since `reset` and `issue` leave a recycled leaf `Init` and readable.

**Higher normative authority:** *ERN — Language Charter v0* (October 27, 2026).  
This specification defines the normative rules of ERN's memory model. Technical names (`derive`, `transfer`, `issue`, etc.) designate **abstract semantic operations**; they do not constitute syntax decisions.

## 36. Shared Mutation and Internal Administration

An abstraction may keep its metadata in `SharedMutable` storage and modify it through `writeShared` to the extent permitted by the applicable rights and contracts. **Shared mutation of metadata does not, however, grant the right to create, recycle, or terminate exclusive authority over the administered storage.** Such operations require `internal` to be exercisable in `Modify` mode from the value administering the storage.

For every administrative abstraction, including arenas, `HandlePool`, and `DataStack`, **`MetaRight` requires `Modify` exercisable on the administering value**. The `writeShared` branch alone is insufficient. `MetaRight` governs the creation or recycling of authorities over existing storage; it does not govern the creation of a fresh allocation by `alloc` (Section 71). Concurrency between calls belongs to Spec 2. Operations issuing, recycling, ending, or invalidating regions must preserve active authorities and dependencies. Allocation through administration shared among simultaneous holders, under an interface not providing such exclusive exercise, cannot be expressed in safe code with only these sequential operations: any synchronized implementation of it belongs to Spec 2. These abstractions remain libraries and add no rights to the kernel.

## 37. Dependent Values and Persistent References

When a value depends on the validity of other storage, that dependency must be carried by an explicit mechanism. In particular, this model retains:

- joint ownership or legal transfer of the resource;
- **non-escaping** dependent values, governed by `depend`, `store`, `AnchorOrder`, and end-of-use operations; they may survive a call if their anchors come from still-valid caller resources;
- library handles checked for identity and generation upon resolution, which are not authorities by themselves;
- validity durations bound to a frame or context, without a universal system of first-class lifetimes;
- safe abstractions encapsulating, when necessary, unsafe operations and proofs of their obligations.

**Not adopted as a universal ERN mechanism:** a first-class persistent reference subject to general lifetime constraints at the type-system level. The above mechanisms are complementary; neither a handle nor a temporary access guarantees the perpetual validity of its target resource on its own.
## 43. Effective Rights and Exercise of Authorities

For an authority `a` and a leaf `l`, `effective(s,a,l)` is derived from the active descendants of `a` whose footprint contains `l`:

1. if `a` is inactive or does not cover `l`, its effective mode is absent;
2. if no active descendant covers `l`, the effective mode is the own mode of `a`;
3. if an active descendant with own mode `Modify` covers `l`, the effective mode of `a` is absent;
4. otherwise, when the covering active descendants are `Observe`, the effective mode of `a` on `l` is `Observe`.

The effect is **local to each leaf**: after splitting a region, the origin may retain effective `Modify` over undistributed leaves.

Requested modes are ordered `Observe ≤ Modify`. `ExercisableAt(s,a,m)` means:

- `a` is active and its own mode permits `m`;
- either `a` is held by the current frame;
- or `a` is held by a place `p`, and the current frame has, over **all** leaves of `p`, an authority itself exercisable in mode `m` with sufficient effective mode.

The latter clause is recursive along the holder chain. Thus, being active or covering a leaf does not automatically make an authority exercisable. `HasRight(s,m,p)` means the current frame has exercise in mode `m` and sufficient effective mode **over every leaf in `p`'s footprint**. Every operation requires the modes it actually needs; an authority's own mode alone is insufficient.

## 44. Dependencies and Effective Anchors

`D(p)` is the set of authorities serving as **validity anchors** for place `p`. An anchor is valid as long as the authority it names is active. Dependencies of contained values are accounted for transitively. Relevant dependencies follow the value during transfer; those of its container do not automatically follow a part transferred in isolation.

For an authority `x`, its **effective anchor** is the root reached by traversing its origin chain. It does not necessarily coincide with its current holder. Lifetime constraints are calculated from the frame of that effective anchor and the frames of places that remain usable. A dependency cannot create a right or artificially extend a lifetime.

`AnchorOrder` requires, for every anchor `x ∈ D(q)` of a usable place `q`, that the frame of the effective anchor of `x` be the frame of `q` or one of its ancestors. `AnchorOrderHeld` imposes the same rule on every **active authority held** by `q`. These conditions apply to the resulting states of operations that move or create holder relations.

## 45. Parameters, Returns, and Reanchoring

A call parameter is an **active derived authority held by the caller** before being passed to the callee; its original provenance may go back to an earlier frame. This interpretation does not require that the authority was originally derived in the calling frame; that additional requirement belongs to Spec 3. The caller **yields** the authority to the new frame: it does not simultaneously retain a copy. If the authority remains in that frame upon return, `exitFrame` releases it; **it is not automatically returned to the caller**. To retain its own right, the caller may pass a **fresh derivative** of the authority it wishes to keep: this is ordinary reborrowing. The definition of ergonomic calling conventions is deferred to Spec 3.

A result is returned by a legal `transfer` into the result place provided by the caller as a `Modify` parameter. Surviving authorities and their dependencies are reanchored by `exitFrame` to still-valid origins. There is no standalone correspondence `M` and no implicit escape permission.

## 56. Uniqueness of Live Administration

**An authority identity may serve as `internal` for at most one live administrative abstraction**, whether an arena, `HandlePool`, `DataStack`, or another library administrative instance. Before registering a new abstraction, its creation operation must jointly check the absence of that identity from **all relevant registries of live administrations**. Uniqueness concerns the identity of the `internal` authority, not merely possible overlap of footprints: abstractions with distinct `internal` identities are not forbidden merely because their footprints overlap. Library contracts must make the information required for this guard available to the creation operation; checking only an abstraction's own registry is insufficient.

**This guard is not a condition for any safety property in Section 57.** The effective right (Section 43, case 3) already prohibits a second issuance over leaves covered by an active block derived from the same authority. Rather, the guard preserves the **abstraction contract**: without it, simultaneous administration of the same `internal` could cause `reject` instead of `fail`, or reissue a previously released block that the first administration still considers unavailable. It creates neither permissions nor allocations and introduces no general detection of authority cycles. Its physical representation and encapsulation of library registries remain outside the kernel.

content.content:
## 58. Transition Outcomes

Every operation has a conceptual outcome among:

```text
Outcome3 = ok(new_state) | reject | fail
```

`reject` means that the static discipline does not permit the step; it is neither an implicit runtime trap nor `ub` in the elementary memory machine. `fail` is a **defined failure** leaving the state unchanged; **only `alloc` may produce it in the O1–O16 kernel**. Other kernel operations produce `ok` or `reject`. Library-abstraction operations, including `issue` (§77), may define their own `fail` cases. Where such failure is provided, static preconditions are checked before dynamic availability, according to the operation's contract.

An `ok` transition must satisfy its preconditions, apply exactly its prescribed effects, and preserve the relevant invariants. No transition fabricates a permission to make its conclusion true. Holder and anchor changes are evaluated in the **resulting state** when a rule explicitly so provides.

## 59. Implicit Preservation of Modes and Anchors

Changes in effective authority are **derived** from active authorities and their origins; no `Suspended` indicator is mutated. Access operations (O9–O11) do not change an anchor without an explicitly authorized effect of transfer, `depend`, `store`, release, or reanchoring. Leaves becoming `Init` do so through a permitted write (`write3`, `writeShared`, `store`, including during a derived `issue`) or a transfer from a corresponding source leaf already `Init`; leaves initialized in `S3.init` are declared as such.

## 60. O1 — Derivation of an Authority

**Preconditions**

1. `source` is an active derived or root authority, and `ExercisableAt(s,source,mode)` holds; its origin chain and anchors are valid: every authority of its origin chain, its effective anchor included, is active.
2. The leaves of `region` exist and belong to the footprint of `source`; `mode` does not exceed the available effective right on these leaves.
3. The addition preserves exclusivity I1: no unrelated active authority becomes incompatible with the derived right, and already-active descendants are respected.
4. The new holding frame is the live current frame. The admissible state's footprint and anchoring restrictions remain true.

**`ok` effect:** A new active authority with fresh identity, origin `source`, requested mode and footprint, and held by the current frame is added. The source remains active; its effective modes are recomputed per leaf. No storage or place anchor is created. Multiple compatible observations remain permitted. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

## 61. O2 — Splitting Authorities

**Preconditions**

1. `source` is active and exercisable by the current frame with sufficient modification rights over the relevant leaves.
2. Each region lies within the available, effectively modifiable footprint of the source.
3. Regions are pairwise disjoint under structural composition or contract `K.DeclaredDisjoint`, subject to obligation `DDSound(K)`; no exclusive right already distributed is overlapped.
4. Creation of the derivatives respects origins, conservation I1/I2, and validity obligations.

**`ok` effect:** An active derived `Modify` authority held by the current frame is created for each region. `source` remains active; its effective modification capability disappears only over distributed leaves and remains on undistributed leaves. Authorities are split logically: `split` performs no physical allocation. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

An unjustified declaration of disjointness may invalidate the proof: without `DDSound`, an accepted `split` may violate I1. Constructing zero-sized subregions is not identified with an allocation of the elementary memory machine; the case of an empty shape in `alloc` is distinct.

## 62. O3 — End of a Derived Borrow

**Preconditions**

1. `authority` is active **and derived**: an authority with no origin is rejected.
2. It is held by the current frame, or by a place `p` on which the current frame has exercisable `Modify`.
3. No active descendant of the authority prevents its release; no other still-usable value may lose a required anchor.
4. If the authority is stored in its holding place, that place is exempted from the check “this authority still appears among the anchors” **only because the effect removes that anchor at the same time**. An anchor with the same identity attached by `depend` to another usable place continues to block the step.
5. Applicable abstraction contracts remain satisfied.

**`ok` effect:** The authority becomes inactive and can no longer be exercised. It is removed from its holding place's anchors when stored there. Effective modes of its origins are recomputed, allowing unblocked rights to return. There is no implicit deallocation. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

# IX. Transfer, Dependencies, and Storage of Rights

These transitions govern value consumption and the controlled movement of their dependencies. A valid transition can neither create an additional permission nor discard a surviving anchor.

## 63. O4 — Consuming Value Transfer

**Preconditions**

1. `source` and `destination` are usable, and the current frame has exercisable `Modify` over their relevant footprints.
2. Source and destination have the **same shape of ordered subtrees**. The `i`-th child of each source part corresponds to the `i`-th child of the corresponding destination part; all nodes are matched. Structural field identity is positional, not an arbitrary matching of children.
3. **All** source leaves are `Init`, and **no** destination leaf is `Init`. The source and destination footprints are disjoint.
4. No exclusive authority is duplicated; validity of derived authorities and active projections is preserved. No active derived authority held outside `source` covers a source leaf, except the authorities through which the step exercises its `Modify` right over `source`: the exercisable authority on which that right rests and its origin chain. Other active authorities remain subject to this check.
5. **No in-place source leaf is pinned**, either statically (`K.Pinned`) or dynamically (`pin`). Storage merely **owned** by the source, which is not itself moved by the transfer of that value, does not prevent this transfer.
6. Dependencies of all still-usable places following the value remain valid; non-escape constraints and `AnchorOrder` are checked in the **resulting state**, including transferred anchors of owned places that remain usable.
7. All moved held authorities, including those of owned storage, satisfy `AnchorOrderHeld` in the resulting state; no authority may escape a local anchor on the grounds that its containing value was transferred.
8. **Local self-blocking prevention:** For each active authority held before the step by a part `r` of `source` whose holder becomes the corresponding part `corr(r)` of `destination`, that authority's footprint contains **no leaf** of `corr(r)` in the resulting state. Transfer is rejected if this local check fails; no global authority-acyclicity check is imposed.
9. **Destination usability:** `destination` is usable in the resulting state.

**`ok` effect:**

- every source leaf becomes `Moved` and each corresponding destination leaf becomes `Init`;
- every authority held by source part `r` acquires as its new holder the corresponding destination part `corr(r)`, not indiscriminately the destination root;
- places owned by `r` become owned by `corr(r)`; their roots follow this owner according to `RootHeld`;
- value dependencies follow the corresponding places under validity guarantees; no authority is created or duplicated;
- destination places receive the transferred values and rights without automatically moving storage not owned by a source part.

**Other outcome:** `reject`. `transfer` to a call result is subject to these same rules.

A partially initialized structure may be transferred **field by field**, but only for fields individually eligible for transfer. This does not automatically destructure a value that owns storage **at the container level**: that storage stays with the container if the container is not transferred. Conversion between structures with permuted fields must be handled separately, not as a `transfer`.

## 64. O5 — Explicit Attachment of an Anchor

**Preconditions**

1. `result` is a usable place over which the current frame has exercisable `Modify`.
2. `anchor` designates an active, valid authority representing a real dependency of the relevant rights or storage; a declared dependency cannot extend an origin's lifetime.
3. Existing anchors are preserved and the addition respects `AnchorOrder`: the effective anchor's frame is the frame of `result` or an ancestor thereof.
4. Every dependency carried by a contained value remains represented in the transitive obligations of its container.

**`ok` effect:** `anchor` is added to `D(result)`; the container's transitive dependencies account for it. No additional access right is created. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

A safe interface must declare dependencies covering those actually required by its implementation; the annotation itself is not presumed true. An unsafe abstraction bears the obligations of its contract.

## 65. O8 — Controlled Storage of an Authority

**Preconditions**

1. `authority` is active, **derived**, and held by the current frame; a root authority can never be stored by `store`.
2. `target` is a usable **leaf** under exercisable `Modify` by the current frame. It holds no other **active** authority. Its data already being `Init` does not by itself prohibit the operation.
3. The stored authority covers neither a leaf of `target` nor the leaves of storage transitively owned by it.
4. The effective anchor of `authority` respects `AnchorOrder` relative to the frame of `target`; other dependencies are preserved.
5. **In the resulting state**, `target` remains under exercisable `Modify` by the current frame (`store_keeps_target_reachable`), and `AnchorOrderHeld` remains true. This is a genuine additional precondition, not an automatic consequence of the preceding ones.

**`ok` effect:** The holder of `authority` becomes `target`; the authority is added to `D(target)`; **only** leaf `target` becomes `Init`. Other fields of a structure, even adjacent ones, do not change their initialization state. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

Overwriting an active authority already held by the leaf is prohibited; its explicit release may make the target reusable. The resulting-state clause does not by itself prohibit all cycles possible after other operations: general freedom from blocking (`NoLock`) is not adopted here.

# X. Reading, Writing, and Initialization

## 69. O12 — Logical End of a Value's Use

**Preconditions**

1. `place` is usable and the current frame has exercisable `Modify` over it.
2. No active descendant over the leaves of `place` **or storage that dies with it** is held outside the places dying with `place`, in a way that would prevent rights from returning or being invalidated. The authorities through which the step exercises its `Modify` right over `place`, namely the exercisable authority on which that right rests and its origin chain, are exempt from this check. Moreover, no authority that the effect makes inactive (held by `place` or by a place dying with it, transitively owned storage included) has an active descendant, whatever its footprint, that the same step does not make inactive.
3. No place **remaining usable after the effect** depends on an authority held by `place`, its root, or an authority that would become inactive when an owned holder dies.
4. **No leaf whose use ends, including transitively owned storage, is pinned**, either statically (`K.Pinned`) or dynamically (`pin`). A dynamic pinning obligation must be legally removed by `unpin` before this step.

**`ok` effect:** The leaves of value `place` become `Uninit`; `place` **remains usable as a place** and may legally be reinitialized. Authorities held by `place` and dead substorages are released; dependencies of the ended value are removed; transitively owned places that cease to live are marked dead. The operation does not automatically trigger physical deallocation in the elementary memory machine: an unfreed allocation may constitute a leak, which this guarantee does not prohibit. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

## 70. O13 — Release of an Owned Storage Unit

**Preconditions**

1. `place` is a **root of storage owned by a value** (`OwnedRoot`), not an ordinary local directly owned by a frame and not part of an aggregate.
2. `K.Deallocable(place)` is established, and `K.FreeCompat(place,auth)` justifies deallocation authority `auth`; this identifier is opaque to the authority kernel.
3. The current frame has exercisable `Modify`; no active derivative over the footprint being freed is held outside holders that die; no surviving place is anchored to an authority of the released region or of its dead holders. The authorities through which the step exercises its `Modify` right over `place`, namely the exercisable authority on which that right rests and its origin chain, are exempt from the check on active derivatives. Moreover, no authority that the effect makes inactive (an authority of the released region, its root included, or an authority whose holder dies) has an active descendant, whatever its footprint, that the same step does not make inactive.
4. No leaf of the released unit is statically or dynamically pinned. Ending external use does not silently turn a still-pinned leaf into a releasable unit.

**`ok` effect:** `place` and the storage that ceases to live are marked dead; authorities of those regions, including their corresponding roots, become inactive, as do authorities whose holders die. Surviving dependencies must remain valid. Every realization of `free` must satisfy the corresponding deallocation relation of the elementary memory machine (Part III). **Other outcome:** `reject`.

## 71. O14 — Allocation of a New Storage Root

**Static preconditions**

1. `shape` is a **nonempty** abstract shape, represented like the local places of `enterFrame`; an allocation of **zero physical size** may be represented by a logical one-leaf shape.
2. The provider is a usable place, and **all leaves of the provider** are `Init`; updates to its metadata are permitted through exercisable `Modify` or a valid `writeShared` over `SharedMutable` metadata.
3. The current frame has exercisable `Modify` over `owner`; new identities and ownership relations must respect `WF3`, `RootHeld`, and liveness restrictions.

**Outcomes**

- `reject`: a static precondition does not hold;
- `fail`: static preconditions hold, but `K.Satisfiable(provider,shape,s)` is false in the state under consideration; **no state change**;
- `ok(s')`: creation of a **new storage root** with fresh identity, owned by `owner`; its leaves start `Uninit`, its new root `Modify` authority with no origin is held by `owner`; provider metadata is updated only in accordance with its modification rights.

Allocation success depends on the provider's state: it does not constitute a right to invent physical memory. Any realization of this operation must satisfy the `AllocStep` relation defined by the rules of Sections 9 and 13.

# XII. Call Frames and Return of Authorities
## 73. O7 — Exiting a Frame

**Preconditions**

1. The current frame is not the initial frame and has a surviving caller.
2. Results that must survive have already been legally transferred to their destinations; no active authority or dependency may remain invalidly attached to locals that are about to die.
3. **No leaf of a place that dies with the frame, including transitively owned storage, is pinned**, either statically (`K.Pinned`) or dynamically (`pin`).
4. Iterated reanchoring of surviving authorities and anchors reaches the **first surviving active origin**, held either by a surviving frame or by a usable place whose terminal owner survives; it is not permitted to skip a surviving origin merely because it is held by a place. The operation is rejected when no suitable surviving origin exists, particularly if the chain reaches a root of the exiting frame.
5. Validity of anchors of surviving values and `AnchorOrderHeld` are checked **in the resulting state**. Other state invariants and resource contracts are respected.

**`ok` effect:**

- the current frame is removed from the stack; its untransferred locals and substorages dying with them become unusable;
- authorities still held by that frame, or by places that have become unusable, are released;
- origins of surviving derived authorities are reanchored to the **first surviving active origin** of their chains, whether held by a frame or a usable place, and the `D` anchors of surviving values are correspondingly reanchored;
- reanchoring changes **neither the footprint nor the own mode** of an authority; parameter identities and relations specific to the frame cease their operational role;
- the calling frame becomes current again.

**Other outcome:** `reject`. Exiting does not entail automatic physical deallocation of all dead places. Deferred cleanup (`defer`) lies outside this kernel. Reanchoring may change the current `origin` relation; protection of a historical borrow lineage during an invocation is a distinct, deferred question.

# XIII. Pinning, Statics, and External Commitments

Pinning forbids certain movements or ends of lifetime. It is not a general guarantee of content immutability.

## 74. O15 — Dynamic Pinning

**Preconditions:** `place` is usable, the current frame has exercisable `Modify` over the relevant leaves, and the operation respects applicable pinning obligations.

**`ok` effect:** A dynamic pinning obligation of fresh identity is installed on the relevant leaves. A leaf is dynamically pinned while at least one active pinning obligation covers it. While an obligation is active, `transfer`, `endUse`, `free`, and `exitFrame` are rejected if they act on leaves it pins; removal of this obligation requires `unpin` under `K.ExternalDone`. Pinning does not make contents immutable. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

## 75. O16 — Removal of Dynamic Pinning

**Preconditions:** `unpin` designates one active dynamic pinning obligation, installed by `pin` on `place`; `place` is usable, the current frame has exercisable `Modify`, and contract `K.ExternalDone`, applied to that obligation, attests that all relevant external use has ended.

**`ok` effect:** The designated dynamic pinning obligation ends, and only that one: a leaf it covered stays pinned while another active obligation covers it. The step does not itself modify values, their initialization, or their access authorities. Static obligations are not removed by this operation. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

**Associated static rule (`StaticPinnedBottom`):** Statics designated by `K.Pinned` must be places **directly** owned by the **base frame**, not merely transitively owned by a static value. This restriction ensures that they do not die when an intermediate frame exits.

# XIV. Arenas and Collective Invalidation — Reference Abstraction

An arena is a **library abstraction**, not a memory-kernel primitive. Operations O17 through O19 are **derived** from operations O1 through O16 and abstraction-specific metadata: `newArena` registers an administration without modifying the kernel; `issue` performs `split` followed by `store` (after checking availability); `reset` performs a `Modify` derivation over all storage—through `derive` or `split`—then `release`, before restoring availability. Their contract below is **normative for the standard-library arena** until Spec 10 takes responsibility for it. It authorizes neither new permissions nor an additional access machine. Arena entries (Section 46) constitute the abstract state of this administration; the guard in Section 56 belongs to its consistency contract. The contracts of `HandlePool` and `DataStack` belong to their library abstractions and are not defined here.

## 76. O17 — Creation of an Administered Arena

**Preconditions**

1. `storage` is an existing, usable place under exercisable `Modify` by the current frame. It may be local, static, allocated, or a block issued by a previous arena.
2. `internal` is explicitly named by the caller, exists, is active, has own mode `Modify`, and `ExercisableAt(s,internal,Modify)` holds.
3. `internal` is **held by a place**: that place is the arena value; `footprint(internal) = footprint(storage)`.
4. **Unified administration guard (Section 56):** no **live** administrative abstraction, whether an arena or a library instance such as a handle pool, already uses this `internal` identity. The relevant registries of library administrations are consulted before registration. Two distinct identities may cover common leaves: this is not in itself grounds for rejection.
5. All leaves of the arena value holding `internal` are already `Init`; construction does not initialize them implicitly.
6. Dependency, holder, storage, and administration relations respect, in the resulting state, `WF3`, I1, `AnchorOrder`, and `AnchorOrderHeld` over the whole kernel state, and the new entry satisfies `ArenaInv` (Section 55).

**`ok` effect:** A live entry `{storage, internal, available, issued}` is added; the initial `available` set represents the administered storage, and `issued` is initially empty. Registering the entry fabricates no place, access right, or `Init` state. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

The identity of `internal`, not the index of `storage`, is the key to preventing duplication of live administrations. No global constraint requires footprints of live arenas to be pairwise disjoint.

## 77. O18 — Issuing an Arena Block

## 85. Splitting a Structure or SoA Columns

Starting from a `Modify` authority exercised over a structure, `split` may provide `Modify` authorities over disjoint leaf regions. Modification of each region is permitted as long as the other validity and holder conditions hold; a second independent derivation over the same leaf does not become legal merely by having a distinct name.

## 86. Arena, Active Views, and Reset

Two disjoint issued regions may be used simultaneously with valid derived rights. `reset` is rejected while an issuance or active dependency would make recycling unsafe; after a legal end of use for all the relevant blocks, the region may be reissued. Reissuance modifies neither the bytes nor the initialization state. A read remains subject to the ordinary conditions of the memory model, notably `Init`, access rights, and representation validity for the requested type. Spec 4 will determine the construction and typing obligations of reissued values.

## 87. Pinning an In-Place Value

A pinned in-place leaf cannot be physically moved by `transfer`. If only an allocation owned by a value is pinned, transfer of that value may remain valid when the other conditions hold, because the owned allocation is not physically moved.

## 88. Local Self-Blocking and Indirect Cycles

An authority stored by `transfer` in a place that would then become its new holder cannot cover any leaf of that place. Likewise, `issue` cannot issue into a leaf belonging to the issued region, **or into a destination that would no longer be exercisable in `Modify` in the resulting state** (O8.5). These restrictions do not promise general freedom from authority cycles: indirect blocking compatible with safety may remain.

## 89. Handles and Persistent References

In a generation-based pool library abstraction, a handle may contain a logical pool identity, an entry identifier, and a generation. This handle is not, by itself, an access right. Safe resolution temporarily supplies authority when the pool and entry are valid; a stale identity or generation leads to defined failure. These conditions belong to the safe abstraction's contract and do not modify the authority-discipline kernel.

/-!
# Handle pool: a library instance of the access discipline (non-normative)

**Non-normative.** This module formalizes the library contract "HandlePool v0.5": the HandlePool
v0.4 annex (items D.1–D.4) as amended by the arbitrations Q3, Q4, Q5 and Q12 (items HP5-1 to
HP5-7) and by the second follow-up to Q3 and Q5 (HP5-1', HP5-1''). `specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.1.md` does not define it (Part XIV preamble: "The
contracts of `HandlePool` and `DataStack` belong to their library abstractions and are not defined
here"). The normative clauses that constrain it are §36 (`MetaRight` is exercisable `Modify` on the
administering value; `writeShared` alone is insufficient; the library adds no rights to the
kernel), §37 and §89 (handles are data, not authorities; a stale identity or generation leads to
defined failure), §38 and §46 (library state outside `S₃`), §47 (empty initial registry), §56 (the
guard over all registries of live administrations), §58 (outcomes) and §76 (the obligations of
`newArena` that `newPool` takes over).

The pool registry lives beside the kernel state (`PState`). Its operations are built on the
kernel operations O1–O16 (§60–§75): `newPool` registers only; `allocSlot` writes the handle into
its destination (O10); `resolve` derives a companion from `internal` over the whole storage, then
an entry authority from the companion (O1 twice); `resolveMany` does the same with `split` (O2) in
`Modify` and with one `Observe` derive per handle (O1) in `Observe`; `unresolve` releases (O3);
`freeSlot` updates the registry only (HP5-1). Every library step is thus, on the kernel side, a
finite sequence of accepted kernel steps (`pstep_kernel`), so, under `DDSound` (§80) and
`StaticsOK` (§47), every kernel state of a library run is kernel-reachable and satisfies the
invariant of §57 (`kernel_guarantee`, HP5-7).
-/

/-- The pool read as an arena entry with nothing available or issued, to reuse `MetaRight` of §36
(HandlePool v0.5, D.3; non-normative library contract). -/
def Pool.entry (pl : Pool) : Arena.ArenaEntry := ⟨pl.storage, pl.internal, [], []⟩

/-- Administration right on the pool (§36; HandlePool v0.5, D.3 corrected by §36, HP5-1;
non-normative library contract): the pool is live (`internal` active) and `MetaRight` holds,
exercisable `Modify` over the pool value; no `writeShared` branch. -/
def AdminRight (s : S3) (pl : Pool) : Prop := s.Active pl.internal ∧ Arena.MetaRight s pl.entry

/-- Decidability of `AdminRight` (§36; HandlePool v0.5, D.3). -/
instance (s : S3) (pl : Pool) : Decidable (AdminRight s pl) := by
  unfold AdminRight; infer_instance

/-- Place of slot `i`, `0` if absent (HandlePool v0.5, D.1; non-normative library contract;
§46). -/
def slotPlace (pl : Pool) (i : Nat) : Nat := ((pl.slots[i]?).map (·.place)).getD 0

/-- The pool with slot `i` replaced (HandlePool v0.5, D.3; non-normative library contract;
§46). -/
def setSlot (pl : Pool) (i : Nat) (sl : Slot) : Pool := { pl with slots := pl.slots.set i sl }

/-! ## `newPool` (HandlePool v0.5, D.1; §56, §76) -/

/-- The pool registry as a registry of live administrations (§56; HandlePool v0.5, D.1;
non-normative library contract): the `internal` identities of its live pools. -/
def liveInternals (s : S3) (pools : List Pool) : List Nat :=
  (pools.filter fun pl => decide (s.Active pl.internal)).map (·.internal)

/-- Preconditions of `newPool(storage, internal)` (HandlePool v0.5, D.1; non-normative library
contract; §56, §76). -/
structure NewPoolPre (s : S3) (pools : List Pool) (others : List (List Nat))
    (storage internal : Nat) : Prop where
  /-- HandlePool v0.5, D.1: "reprend les autres obligations applicables de `newArena`"
  (§76.1–§76.3, §76.5, §76.6, read on the resulting state as v0.1 §76.6 states it). -/
  base : Arena.NewArenaBase s storage internal
  /-- HandlePool v0.5, D.1: every leaf of the input storage is `Uninit`. -/
  uninit : ∀ l ∈ footprint s.P storage, s.I l = .uninit
  /-- HandlePool v0.5, D.1, §56: `internal` is absent from the pool registry and from every other
  registry of live administrations `others`. -/
  guard : Arena.Guard56 (liveInternals s pools :: others) internal

/-- Decidability of `NewPoolPre` (HandlePool v0.5, D.1; §56, §76). -/
instance (s : S3) (pools : List Pool) (others : List (List Nat)) (storage internal : Nat) :
    Decidable (NewPoolPre s pools others storage internal) :=
  decidable_of_iff (Arena.NewArenaBase s storage internal ∧
    (∀ l ∈ footprint s.P storage, s.I l = .uninit) ∧
    Arena.Guard56 (liveInternals s pools :: others) internal)
    ⟨fun ⟨a, b, c⟩ => ⟨a, b, c⟩, fun ⟨a, b, c⟩ => ⟨a, b, c⟩⟩

/-- Effect of `newPool` (HandlePool v0.5, D.1; non-normative library contract): a pool with the
fresh identity `nId`, one free slot of generation zero per child of the storage, the kernel state
unchanged (§46, §76). -/
def newPoolEff (L : PState) (storage internal : Nat) : PState :=
  { L with
    pools := L.pools ++ [⟨L.nId, storage, internal,
      (kids L.kern.P storage).map fun q => ⟨q, 0, false⟩⟩]
    nId := L.nId + 1 }

/-- `newPool` as a relation (HandlePool v0.5, D.1; §58; non-normative library contract): `ok` or
`reject`; `others` are the other registries of live administrations (§56). -/
def NewPoolStep (others : List (List Nat)) (storage internal : Nat) (L : PState) :
    Outcome3 PState → Prop :=
  Guarded (NewPoolPre L.kern L.pools others storage internal) (newPoolEff L storage internal)

/-! ## `allocSlot` (HandlePool v0.5, D.3) -/

/-- Static preconditions of `allocSlot(pool, dst)` (HandlePool v0.5, D.3 corrected by §36;
non-normative library contract). "Apte à recevoir la représentation d'un handle" names no state
component and is not represented. -/
structure AllocSlotStatic (s : S3) (pl : Pool) (dst : Nat) : Prop where
  /-- HandlePool v0.5, D.3, §36: live pool and `MetaRight`. -/
  right : AdminRight s pl
  /-- HandlePool v0.5, D.3: `dst` is usable. -/
  dstUsable : s.Usable dst
  /-- HandlePool v0.5, D.3: `dst` is a leaf (the handle is written into "la seule feuille
  `dst`"). -/
  dstLeaf : isLeaf s.P dst
  /-- HandlePool v0.5, D.3 with §67.1: the write of the handle needs exercisable `Modify` over
  `dst`. -/
  dstRight : HasRight s .modify dst
  /-- HandlePool v0.5, D.3: `dst` is not `Init`. -/
  dstNotInit : s.I dst ≠ .init
  /-- HandlePool v0.5, D.3: `dst` holds no active authority. -/
  dstFree : ∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length,
    OptP (s.A[j]?) (fun z => z.active = true → z.holder ≠ .place dst) True

/-- Decidability of `AllocSlotStatic` (HandlePool v0.5, D.3; §36, §67). -/
instance (s : S3) (pl : Pool) (dst : Nat) : Decidable (AllocSlotStatic s pl dst) :=
  decidable_of_iff (AdminRight s pl ∧ s.Usable dst ∧ isLeaf s.P dst ∧ HasRight s .modify dst ∧
    s.I dst ≠ .init ∧ ∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length,
      OptP (s.A[j]?) (fun z => z.active = true → z.holder ≠ .place dst) True)
    ⟨fun ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f⟩ => ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f⟩, fun ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f⟩ => ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f⟩⟩

/-- Effect of `allocSlot` on slot `i` of pool `j` (HandlePool v0.5, D.3; non-normative library
contract): the slot becomes live with its generation kept; the handle is written into the leaf
`dst`, which alone becomes `Init` (§67 effect). -/
def allocSlotEff (L : PState) (j : Nat) (pl : Pool) (i : Nat) (sl : Slot) (dst : Nat) : PState :=
  { L with
    kern := write3Eff L.kern [dst]
    pools := L.pools.set j (setSlot pl i { sl with live := true }) }

/-- The handle written by `allocSlot` for slot `i` (HandlePool v0.5, D.3; non-normative library
contract; §37, §89). -/
def slotHandle (pl : Pool) (i : Nat) : Option Handle :=
  (pl.slots[i]?).map fun sl => ⟨pl.id, i, sl.gen⟩

/-- `allocSlot(pool j, dst)` as a relation (HandlePool v0.5, D.3; §58; non-normative library
contract): `reject` without the pool or a static precondition; then `fail` when no slot is free;
`ok` on any free slot. -/
inductive AllocSlotStep (j dst : Nat) (L : PState) : Outcome3 PState → Prop where
  | noPool : L.pools[j]? = none → AllocSlotStep j dst L .reject
  | static {pl : Pool} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → ¬ AllocSlotStatic L.kern pl dst →
      AllocSlotStep j dst L .reject
  | fail {pl : Pool} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → AllocSlotStatic L.kern pl dst →
      (∀ sl ∈ pl.slots, sl.live = true) → AllocSlotStep j dst L .fail
  | ok {pl : Pool} {i : Nat} {sl : Slot} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → AllocSlotStatic L.kern pl dst →
      pl.slots[i]? = some sl → sl.live = false →
      AllocSlotStep j dst L (.ok (allocSlotEff L j pl i sl dst))

/-! ## `resolve`, `resolveMany` (HandlePool v0.5, D.2, HP5-5, HP5-6) -/

/-- Validity of a handle for pool `pl` (HandlePool v0.5, D.2, D.3, HP5-5, HP5-6, HP5-1''; §89;
non-normative library contract): the pool is live (`internal` active, §46 analogue: a handle of a
dead pool is stale, HP5-5), the handle names the pool, and it designates a live slot at its
generation (a handle of a free entry is stale, HP5-6); a slot index outside the pool designates
nothing. -/
def HandleOK (s : S3) (pl : Pool) (h : Handle) : Prop :=
  s.Active pl.internal ∧ h.id = pl.id ∧
    OptP (pl.slots[h.slot]?) (fun sl => sl.gen = h.gen ∧ sl.live = true) False

/-- Decidability of `HandleOK` (HandlePool v0.5, D.2; §89). -/
instance (s : S3) (pl : Pool) (h : Handle) : Decidable (HandleOK s pl h) := by
  unfold HandleOK; infer_instance

/-- Legal exercise of `internal` at mode `m` for the companion (HandlePool v0.5, D.2;
non-normative library contract): the preconditions of the `derive` of the companion from
`internal` over all leaves of the storage (§60). -/
def ResolveRight (s : S3) (pl : Pool) (m : Mode) : Prop :=
  DerivePre s pl.internal (footprint s.P pl.storage) m

/-- Decidability of `ResolveRight` (HandlePool v0.5, D.2; §60). -/
instance (s : S3) (pl : Pool) (m : Mode) : Decidable (ResolveRight s pl m) := by
  unfold ResolveRight; infer_instance

/-- State after the companion (HandlePool v0.5, D.2; §60 effect; non-normative library contract):
authority `|A|`, derived from `internal` at mode `m` over all leaves of the storage. -/
def compS (s : S3) (pl : Pool) (m : Mode) : S3 :=
  deriveEff s pl.internal (footprint s.P pl.storage) m

/-- Observe derivations from `c`, one per region in order (HandlePool v0.5, D.2: `resolveMany` in
`Observe`; §60; non-normative library contract): each accepted in the state left by the previous
ones. -/
def DerivesPre (s : S3) (c : Nat) : List (List Nat) → Prop
  | [] => True
  | r :: rs => DerivePre s c r .observe ∧ DerivesPre (deriveEff s c r .observe) c rs

/-- Decidability of `DerivesPre` (HandlePool v0.5, D.2, §60). -/
instance decDerivesPre (s : S3) (c : Nat) :
    (rs : List (List Nat)) → Decidable (DerivesPre s c rs)
  | [] => isTrue trivial
  | r :: rs =>
    have := decDerivesPre (deriveEff s c r .observe) c rs
    inferInstanceAs (Decidable (_ ∧ _))

/-- Effect of the `Observe` derivations from `c`, in order (HandlePool v0.5, D.2; §60 effect). -/
def derivesEff (s : S3) (c : Nat) : List (List Nat) → S3
  | [] => s
  | r :: rs => derivesEff (deriveEff s c r .observe) c rs

/-- Entry authorities of a batch from the companion `c` (HandlePool v0.5, D.2; non-normative
library contract): `split` (§61) in `Modify`, successive `Observe` derivations (§60) in
`Observe`. -/
def EntriesPre (k : K) : Mode → S3 → Nat → List (List Nat) → Prop
  | .modify, s, c, rs => SplitPre k s c rs
  | .observe, s, c, rs => DerivesPre s c rs

/-- Decidability of `EntriesPre` (HandlePool v0.5, D.2; §60, §61). -/
instance (k : K) [∀ r r', Decidable (k.DeclaredDisjoint r r')] (m : Mode) (s : S3) (c : Nat)
    (rs : List (List Nat)) : Decidable (EntriesPre k m s c rs) := by
  cases m <;> unfold EntriesPre <;> infer_instance

/-- Effect of the entry authorities of a batch (HandlePool v0.5, D.2; §60, §61 effects). -/
def entriesEff : Mode → S3 → Nat → List (List Nat) → S3
  | .modify, s, c, rs => splitEff s c rs
  | .observe, s, c, rs => derivesEff s c rs

/-- Regions of the entries designated by a batch: the footprint of each slot (HandlePool v0.5,
D.2; non-normative library contract; §60). -/
def entryRegions (s : S3) (pl : Pool) (hs : List Handle) : List (List Nat) :=
  hs.map fun h => footprint s.P (slotPlace pl h.slot)

/-- Ghost entries of a batch: the `n`-th entry authority is `c + 1 + n`, for slot and generation of
the `n`-th handle (HandlePool v0.5, D.2; auxiliary, §38). -/
def batchEntries (c : Nat) (hs : List Handle) : List (Nat × Nat × Nat) :=
  mapI (fun i h => (i, h.slot, h.gen)) (c + 1) hs

/-- `resolve(h, m)` on pool `j` as a relation (HandlePool v0.5, D.2, HP5-5, HP5-6; §58, §89;
non-normative library contract): `reject` without the pool; then `fail` for a handle of a dead
pool, of another pool, stale, absent or free, before the right is checked (HP5-5); then `reject`
without the legal exercise of `internal`; then the companion and the entry authority derived from
it, `reject` when the second derivation is not accepted. -/
inductive ResolveStep (j : Nat) (h : Handle) (m : Mode) (L : PState) : Outcome3 PState → Prop where
  | noPool : L.pools[j]? = none → ResolveStep j h m L .reject
  | fail {pl : Pool} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → ¬ HandleOK L.kern pl h →
      ResolveStep j h m L .fail
  | noRight {pl : Pool} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → HandleOK L.kern pl h →
      ¬ ResolveRight L.kern pl m → ResolveStep j h m L .reject
  | noEntry {pl : Pool} {sl : Slot} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → HandleOK L.kern pl h →
      ResolveRight L.kern pl m → pl.slots[h.slot]? = some sl →
      ¬ DerivePre (compS L.kern pl m) L.kern.A.length (footprint L.kern.P sl.place) m →
      ResolveStep j h m L .reject
  | ok {pl : Pool} {sl : Slot} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → HandleOK L.kern pl h →
      ResolveRight L.kern pl m → pl.slots[h.slot]? = some sl →
      DerivePre (compS L.kern pl m) L.kern.A.length (footprint L.kern.P sl.place) m →
      ResolveStep j h m L (.ok { L with
        kern := deriveEff (compS L.kern pl m) L.kern.A.length (footprint L.kern.P sl.place) m
        res := L.res ++ [⟨pl.id, pl.internal, L.kern.A.length, m,
          [(L.kern.A.length + 1, h.slot, h.gen)]⟩] })

/-- Validity of a batch (HandlePool v0.5, D.2, HP5-5; non-normative library contract): every
handle is valid (`HandleOK`); pairwise distinct slots in `Modify` only (§58, §89). -/
def BatchOK (s : S3) (pl : Pool) (hs : List Handle) (m : Mode) : Prop :=
  (∀ h ∈ hs, HandleOK s pl h) ∧ (m = .modify → (hs.map (·.slot)).Nodup)

/-- Decidability of `BatchOK` (HandlePool v0.5, D.2; §58, §89). -/
instance (s : S3) (pl : Pool) (hs : List Handle) (m : Mode) : Decidable (BatchOK s pl hs m) := by
  unfold BatchOK; infer_instance

/-- `resolveMany(hs, m)` on pool `j` as a relation (HandlePool v0.5, D.2, HP5-5; §58;
non-normative library contract): `reject` without the pool; then an atomic `fail` for an invalid
batch, before the right is checked (HP5-5); then `reject` without the legal exercise of
`internal`; then one companion and the entry authorities (`EntriesPre`), `reject` when they are
not accepted. -/
inductive ResolveManyStep (k : K) (j : Nat) (hs : List Handle) (m : Mode) (L : PState) :
    Outcome3 PState → Prop where
  | noPool : L.pools[j]? = none → ResolveManyStep k j hs m L .reject
  | fail {pl : Pool} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → ¬ BatchOK L.kern pl hs m →
      ResolveManyStep k j hs m L .fail
  | noRight {pl : Pool} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → BatchOK L.kern pl hs m →
      ¬ ResolveRight L.kern pl m → ResolveManyStep k j hs m L .reject
  | noEntries {pl : Pool} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → BatchOK L.kern pl hs m →
      ResolveRight L.kern pl m →
      ¬ EntriesPre k m (compS L.kern pl m) L.kern.A.length (entryRegions L.kern pl hs) →
      ResolveManyStep k j hs m L .reject
  | ok {pl : Pool} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → BatchOK L.kern pl hs m → ResolveRight L.kern pl m →
      EntriesPre k m (compS L.kern pl m) L.kern.A.length (entryRegions L.kern pl hs) →
      ResolveManyStep k j hs m L (.ok { L with
        kern := entriesEff m (compS L.kern pl m) L.kern.A.length (entryRegions L.kern pl hs)
        res := L.res ++ [⟨pl.id, pl.internal, L.kern.A.length, m,
          batchEntries L.kern.A.length hs⟩] })

/-! ## `unresolve` (HandlePool v0.5, D.2) -/

/-- Releases the authorities of a list in order (§62); `none` as soon as one release is not
accepted (HandlePool v0.5, D.2: "Les règles de `release` … restent applicables"). -/
def releaseAll : S3 → List Nat → Option S3
  | s, [] => some s
  | s, a :: l => if ReleasePre s a then releaseAll (releaseEff s a) l else none

/-- The resolution of companion `c` (HandlePool v0.5, D.2; ghost lookup, §38). -/
def findRes (L : PState) (c : Nat) : Option Res := L.res.find? fun r => r.comp == c

/-- Authorities released by `unresolve` of `r` (HandlePool v0.5, D.2; non-normative library
contract): the entry authorities still active, then the companion (§62). -/
def unresolveList (s : S3) (r : Res) : List Nat :=
  ((r.entries.map (·.1)).filter fun a => decide (s.Active a)) ++ [r.comp]

/-- `unresolve(c)` as a relation (HandlePool v0.5, D.2; §58; non-normative library contract): the
releases of `unresolveList`; `reject` when one is not accepted or `c` is no companion. -/
inductive UnresolveStep (c : Nat) (L : PState) : Outcome3 PState → Prop where
  | none : findRes L c = none → UnresolveStep c L .reject
  | reject {r : Res} : findRes L c = some r → releaseAll L.kern (unresolveList L.kern r) = none →
      UnresolveStep c L .reject
  | ok {r : Res} {s' : S3} : findRes L c = some r →
      releaseAll L.kern (unresolveList L.kern r) = some s' →
      UnresolveStep c L (.ok { L with kern := s' })

/-! ## `freeSlot` (HandlePool v0.5, D.3 as amended by HP5-1, HP5-1', HP5-1'') -/

/-- No active strict descendant of the `internal` of pool `pl` covers a leaf of place `q`
(HandlePool v0.5, HP5-1 as amended by HP5-1': "aucune autorité active, descendante stricte de
internal de ce pool, ne couvre l'entrée"; §42: descendants along the current origin chain, which
covers the reanchoring of §73.4 onto `internal`; non-normative library contract). -/
def NoInternalDesc (s : S3) (pl : Pool) (q : Nat) : Prop :=
  ∀ x ∈ List.range s.A.length, s.Active x → pl.internal ∈ s.ancs x →
    ∀ l ∈ s.afp x, l ∉ footprint s.P q

/-- Decidability of `NoInternalDesc` (HandlePool v0.5, HP5-1'; §42). -/
instance (s : S3) (pl : Pool) (q : Nat) : Decidable (NoInternalDesc s pl q) := by
  unfold NoInternalDesc; infer_instance

/-- Content conditions of `freeSlot` on slot place `q` of pool `pl` (HandlePool v0.5, HP5-1,
HP5-1'; non-normative library contract; §41, §42). -/
structure FreeContentOK (L : PState) (pl : Pool) (q : Nat) : Prop where
  /-- HandlePool v0.5, HP5-1: no leaf of the entry is `Init`; each is `Uninit` or `Moved`
  (§41). -/
  notInit : ∀ l ∈ footprint L.kern.P q, L.kern.I l ≠ .init
  /-- HandlePool v0.5, HP5-1': no active strict descendant of `internal` of this pool covers a
  leaf of the entry (§42). -/
  noDesc : NoInternalDesc L.kern pl q

/-- Decidability of `FreeContentOK` (HandlePool v0.5, HP5-1, HP5-1'; §41, §42). -/
instance (L : PState) (pl : Pool) (q : Nat) : Decidable (FreeContentOK L pl q) :=
  decidable_of_iff ((∀ l ∈ footprint L.kern.P q, L.kern.I l ≠ .init) ∧ NoInternalDesc L.kern pl q)
    ⟨fun ⟨a, b⟩ => ⟨a, b⟩, fun ⟨a, b⟩ => ⟨a, b⟩⟩

/-- Effect of `freeSlot` on slot `i` of pool `j` (HandlePool v0.5, HP5-1; non-normative library
contract): the slot becomes free and its generation is incremented; there is no end-of-use effect
and the kernel state is unchanged (§36: the library adds no rights to the kernel). -/
def freeSlotEff (L : PState) (j : Nat) (pl : Pool) (i : Nat) (sl : Slot) : PState :=
  { L with pools := L.pools.set j (setSlot pl i ⟨sl.place, sl.gen + 1, false⟩) }

/-- `freeSlot(h)` on pool `j` as a relation (HandlePool v0.5, D.3 corrected by §36, HP5-1; outcome
order of HP5-1'' (Q5 extended to `freeSlot`); §58, §89; non-normative library contract): `reject`
without the pool; then `fail` for a handle of a dead pool, of another pool, stale, absent or free,
before the right is checked; then `reject` without the administration right (live pool and
`MetaRight`); then `reject` unless the content conditions hold (`FreeContentOK`); then `ok`. -/
inductive FreeSlotStep (j : Nat) (h : Handle) (L : PState) : Outcome3 PState → Prop where
  | noPool : L.pools[j]? = none → FreeSlotStep j h L .reject
  | fail {pl : Pool} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → ¬ HandleOK L.kern pl h → FreeSlotStep j h L .fail
  | noRight {pl : Pool} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → HandleOK L.kern pl h → ¬ AdminRight L.kern pl →
      FreeSlotStep j h L .reject
  | noContent {pl : Pool} {sl : Slot} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → HandleOK L.kern pl h →
      AdminRight L.kern pl → pl.slots[h.slot]? = some sl → ¬ FreeContentOK L pl sl.place →
      FreeSlotStep j h L .reject
  | ok {pl : Pool} {sl : Slot} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → HandleOK L.kern pl h →
      AdminRight L.kern pl → pl.slots[h.slot]? = some sl → FreeContentOK L pl sl.place →
      FreeSlotStep j h L (.ok (freeSlotEff L j pl h.slot sl))

/-! ## Library runs (HandlePool v0.5; §38, §46, §47) -/

/-- One `ok` step of a library run (HandlePool v0.5; non-normative library contract): a kernel
step O1–O16 of non-administrative code, the registry unchanged, or an accepted pool operation
(§58). -/
inductive PStep (k : K) : PState → PState → Prop where
  | kernel {L : PState} {s' : S3} : KStep k L.kern s' → PStep k L { L with kern := s' }
  | newPool {L L' : PState} {others : List (List Nat)} {st i : Nat} :

/-- A handle of a dead pool is not valid (HandlePool v0.5, HP5-5; §46 analogue, §89). -/
theorem not_handleOK_dead {s : S3} {pl : Pool} {h : Handle} (hd : ¬ s.Active pl.internal) :
    ¬ HandleOK s pl h :=
  fun ⟨ha, _⟩ => hd ha

/-- A handle of another pool is not valid (HandlePool v0.5, D.2, D.3; §89). -/
theorem not_handleOK_other {s : S3} {pl : Pool} {h : Handle} (hid : h.id ≠ pl.id) :
    ¬ HandleOK s pl h :=
  fun ⟨_, e, _⟩ => hid e

/-- A stale handle is not valid (HandlePool v0.5, D.2, D.3; §89). -/
theorem not_handleOK_stale {s : S3} {pl : Pool} {h : Handle} {sl : Slot}
    (hsl : pl.slots[h.slot]? = some sl) (hg : sl.gen ≠ h.gen) : ¬ HandleOK s pl h :=
  fun ⟨_, _, ho⟩ => by rw [hsl] at ho; exact hg ho.1

/-- A handle of a free slot is not valid, even at the slot's generation (HandlePool v0.5, D.2:
"slot … libre ⇒ `fail`", HP5-6; §89). -/
theorem not_handleOK_free {s : S3} {pl : Pool} {h : Handle} {sl : Slot}
    (hsl : pl.slots[h.slot]? = some sl) (hf : sl.live = false) : ¬ HandleOK s pl h :=
  fun ⟨_, _, ho⟩ => by rw [hsl] at ho; have h2 := ho.2; rw [hf] at h2; cases h2

/-- A handle of an absent slot is not valid (HandlePool v0.5, D.2: "slot absent ⇒ `fail`";
§89). -/
theorem not_handleOK_absent {s : S3} {pl : Pool} {h : Handle} (hn : pl.slots[h.slot]? = none) :
    ¬ HandleOK s pl h :=
  fun ⟨_, _, ho⟩ => by rw [hn] at ho; exact ho

/-- An invalid handle makes `resolve` fail, before the right is checked, and `fail` is its only
outcome (HandlePool v0.5, D.2: "⇒ `fail`, sans changement d'état"; HP5-5; §58). -/
theorem pool_resolve_invalid_fails {L : PState} {j : Nat} {pl : Pool} {h : Handle} {m : Mode}
    (hp : L.pools[j]? = some pl) (hH : ¬ HandleOK L.kern pl h) :
    ResolveStep j h m L .fail ∧ ∀ o, ResolveStep j h m L o → o = .fail := by
  refine ⟨.fail hp hH, fun o ho => ?_⟩
  cases ho with
  | noPool hn => rw [hp] at hn; cases hn
  | fail => rfl
  | noRight hp' hH' => rw [hp] at hp'; cases hp'; exact absurd hH' hH
  | noEntry hp' hH' => rw [hp] at hp'; cases hp'; exact absurd hH' hH
  | ok hp' hH' => rw [hp] at hp'; cases hp'; exact absurd hH' hH

/-- `pool_resolve_stale_fails` (HandlePool v0.5, D.2, HP5-5; §89: "a stale identity or generation
leads to defined failure"): whatever the right, a handle of a former generation makes `resolve`
fail. -/
theorem pool_resolve_stale_fails {L : PState} {j : Nat} {pl : Pool} {h : Handle} {m : Mode}
    {sl : Slot} (hp : L.pools[j]? = some pl) (hsl : pl.slots[h.slot]? = some sl)
    (hg : sl.gen ≠ h.gen) :
    ResolveStep j h m L .fail ∧ ∀ o, ResolveStep j h m L o → o = .fail :=
  pool_resolve_invalid_fails hp (not_handleOK_stale hsl hg)

/-- `pool_resolve_other_pool_fails` (HandlePool v0.5, D.2, HP5-5; §89). -/
theorem pool_resolve_other_pool_fails {L : PState} {j : Nat} {pl : Pool} {h : Handle} {m : Mode}
    (hp : L.pools[j]? = some pl) (hid : h.id ≠ pl.id) :
    ResolveStep j h m L .fail ∧ ∀ o, ResolveStep j h m L o → o = .fail :=
  pool_resolve_invalid_fails hp (not_handleOK_other hid)

/-- A handle of a dead pool (`internal` inactive) is stale: `resolve` fails (HandlePool v0.5,
HP5-5; §89). -/
theorem pool_resolve_dead_fails {L : PState} {j : Nat} {pl : Pool} {h : Handle} {m : Mode}
    (hp : L.pools[j]? = some pl) (hd : ¬ L.kern.Active pl.internal) :
    ResolveStep j h m L .fail ∧ ∀ o, ResolveStep j h m L o → o = .fail :=
  pool_resolve_invalid_fails hp (not_handleOK_dead hd)

/-- A handle of a free entry is stale: `resolve` fails (HandlePool v0.5, HP5-6; §89). -/
theorem pool_resolve_free_fails {L : PState} {j : Nat} {pl : Pool} {h : Handle} {m : Mode}
    {sl : Slot} (hp : L.pools[j]? = some pl) (hsl : pl.slots[h.slot]? = some sl)
    (hf : sl.live = false) :
    ResolveStep j h m L .fail ∧ ∀ o, ResolveStep j h m L o → o = .fail :=
  pool_resolve_invalid_fails hp (not_handleOK_free hsl hf)

/-- An invalid handle, a handle of a dead pool included, makes `freeSlot` fail, before the right is
checked, and `fail` is its only outcome (HandlePool v0.5, D.3: "`fail` si l'identité ou la
génération ne correspond pas; un slot déjà libre n'est pas rendu libérable par cette seule
égalité"; HP5-1''; §58, §89). -/
theorem pool_freeSlot_invalid_fails {L : PState} {j : Nat} {pl : Pool} {h : Handle}
    (hp : L.pools[j]? = some pl) (hH : ¬ HandleOK L.kern pl h) :
    FreeSlotStep j h L .fail ∧ ∀ o, FreeSlotStep j h L o → o = .fail := by
  refine ⟨.fail hp hH, fun o ho => ?_⟩
  cases ho with
  | noPool hn => rw [hp] at hn; cases hn
  | fail => rfl
  | noRight hp' hH' => rw [hp] at hp'; cases hp'; exact absurd hH' hH
  | noContent hp' hH' => rw [hp] at hp'; cases hp'; exact absurd hH' hH
  | ok hp' hH' => rw [hp] at hp'; cases hp'; exact absurd hH' hH

/-- `freeSlot` of a stale handle, of a handle of another pool, or of a free slot at its generation
fails, whatever the right (HandlePool v0.5, D.3, HP5-1''; §58, §89). -/
theorem pool_freeSlot_stale_other_free_fails {L : PState} {j : Nat} {pl : Pool} {h : Handle}
    {sl : Slot} (hp : L.pools[j]? = some pl) (hsl : pl.slots[h.slot]? = some sl) :
    (sl.gen ≠ h.gen ∨ h.id ≠ pl.id ∨ sl.live = false) →
      FreeSlotStep j h L .fail ∧ ∀ o, FreeSlotStep j h L o → o = .fail := by
  rintro (hg | hid | hf)
  · exact pool_freeSlot_invalid_fails hp (not_handleOK_stale hsl hg)
  · exact pool_freeSlot_invalid_fails hp (not_handleOK_other hid)
  · exact pool_freeSlot_invalid_fails hp (not_handleOK_free hsl hf)

/-- A handle of a dead pool (`internal` inactive) is stale: `freeSlot` fails (HandlePool v0.5,
HP5-1''; §89). -/
theorem pool_freeSlot_dead_fails {L : PState} {j : Nat} {pl : Pool} {h : Handle}
    (hp : L.pools[j]? = some pl) (hd : ¬ L.kern.Active pl.internal) :
    FreeSlotStep j h L .fail ∧ ∀ o, FreeSlotStep j h L o → o = .fail :=
  pool_freeSlot_invalid_fails hp (not_handleOK_dead hd)

/-- A missing pool index makes `freeSlot` reject, and `reject` is its only outcome
(HandlePool v0.5, HP5-1''; §58). -/
theorem pool_freeSlot_missing_rejects {L : PState} {j : Nat} {h : Handle}
    (hn : L.pools[j]? = none) : ∀ o, FreeSlotStep j h L o → o = .reject := by
  intro o ho
  cases ho with
  | noPool => rfl
  | fail hp => cases hp.symm.trans hn
  | noRight hp => cases hp.symm.trans hn
  | noContent hp => cases hp.symm.trans hn
  | ok hp => cases hp.symm.trans hn

/-- With a valid handle, `freeSlot` without the administration right rejects, and `reject` is its
only outcome (HandlePool v0.5, D.3 corrected by §36, HP5-1''; §58). -/
theorem pool_freeSlot_noRight_rejects {L : PState} {j : Nat} {pl : Pool} {h : Handle}
    (hp : L.pools[j]? = some pl) (hH : HandleOK L.kern pl h) (hR : ¬ AdminRight L.kern pl) :
    FreeSlotStep j h L .reject ∧ ∀ o, FreeSlotStep j h L o → o = .reject := by
  refine ⟨.noRight hp hH hR, fun o ho => ?_⟩
  cases ho with
  | noPool => rfl
  | fail hp' hn => rw [hp] at hp'; cases hp'; exact absurd hH hn
  | noRight => rfl
  | noContent => rfl
  | ok hp' _ hR' => rw [hp] at hp'; cases hp'; exact absurd hR' hR

/-- With a valid handle and the administration right, `freeSlot` rejects when the content
conditions fail, and `reject` is its only outcome (HandlePool v0.5, HP5-1, HP5-1', HP5-1''; §58). -/
theorem pool_freeSlot_content_rejects {L : PState} {j : Nat} {pl : Pool} {h : Handle} {sl : Slot}
    (hp : L.pools[j]? = some pl) (hH : HandleOK L.kern pl h) (hR : AdminRight L.kern pl)
    (hsl : pl.slots[h.slot]? = some sl) (hc : ¬ FreeContentOK L pl sl.place) :
    FreeSlotStep j h L .reject ∧ ∀ o, FreeSlotStep j h L o → o = .reject := by
  refine ⟨.noContent hp hH hR hsl hc, fun o ho => ?_⟩
  cases ho with
  | noPool => rfl
  | fail hp' hn => rw [hp] at hp'; cases hp'; exact absurd hH hn
  | noRight => rfl
  | noContent => rfl
  | ok hp' _ _ hsl' hc' =>
    rw [hp] at hp'; cases hp'; rw [hsl] at hsl'; cases hsl'; exact absurd hc' hc

/-! ## `resolveMany`: atomicity and distinctness (HandlePool v0.5, D.2, HP5-5) -/

/-- An invalid batch makes `resolveMany` fail, before the right is checked, and `fail` is its only
outcome: no partial creation of rights (HandlePool v0.5, D.2: "`fail` atomique"; HP5-5; §58). -/
theorem pool_resolveMany_invalid_fails {k : K} {L : PState} {j : Nat} {pl : Pool}

  | noRight hp' hB' => rw [hp] at hp'; cases hp'; exact absurd hB' hB
  | noEntries hp' hB' => rw [hp] at hp'; cases hp'; exact absurd hB' hB
  | ok hp' hB' => rw [hp] at hp'; cases hp'; exact absurd hB' hB

theorem pool_resolve_missing_rejects {k : K} {L : PState} {j : Nat} (hn : L.pools[j]? = none) :

    | noRight hp => cases hp.symm.trans hn
    | noEntries hp => cases hp.symm.trans hn
    | ok hp => cases hp.symm.trans hn
